scope: Corollary 15.4 (Undecidability of finite subgroup-interval recognition) of the manuscript “Finite congruence lattices: characterization and undecidability” (preprints/Finite-Congruence-Lattices-Characterization-and-Undecidability-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 206 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d26d6cd6285de4f2), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 158. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is no deterministic Turing machine which, given the order table of a finite nonempty lattice L, always halts and decides whether L ∼ = [H, G] for some finite group G and subgroup H ≤ G, where [H, G] consists of every subgroup K with H ≤ K ≤ G, ordered by inclusion. Equivalently, there is no total computable bound, in terms of lattice cardinality, on the least possible order of the top group G among lattices admitting such a realization.
